The alloy PWA 1480 is a nickel-base superalloy.
The tensile tests were conducted in the range from 20-1093°C.
The strain rate range of the tensile tests was 0.5 and 50%/min.
The yield strength of the alloy is constant from 20 to 760°C.
Deformation is dominated by y1 shearing by pairs of {111}a/2<110> dislocations at low temperatures.
The activation energy for yielding is zero at low temperatures.
Deformation is dominated by y* by-pass at high temperatures.
The true activation energy for yielding is 500 kJ/mol at high temperatures.
The deformation mechanism at intermediate temperatures is transitional.
The Brown-Ham model is a micro-mechanical model of the yielding process.
The Ardell model is a modification of the Brown-Ham model for high Vf alloys.
The Huther-Reppich model is a model for high Vf alloys that allows for a transition from 'weak' to 'strong' dislocation pair coupling.
The Copley-Kear model is a model for alloys such as Mar-M 200 that assumes penetration of the first dislocation into the particle is the rate-limiting step.
The Brown-Ham by-pass model is a model for precipitate by-pass by dislocations at high temperatures.
The mismatch effects between the y and y1 phases were not considered in the models discussed in the paper.
